def: The order SQL clauses take effect: FROM/JOIN, WHERE, GROUP BY, HAVING, SELECT (window functions), DISTINCT, ORDER BY, LIMIT. Explains why SELECT aliases are not visible in WHERE.
A filter on groups, applied after GROUP BY and the aggregates; WHERE filters rows before grouping.
An aggregate or ranking computed over a partition of rows while keeping every row, written f(...) OVER (PARTITION BY ... ORDER BY ...).
A named subquery introduced with WITH, used to write a query as readable steps.
An extreme value inflates the mean and standard deviation of its own group so much that a z-score rule cannot flag it; with n points |z| can never exceed (n−1)/√n.
Read from the cache, fall back to the database and fill the cache on a miss; on writes update the database and delete the cache key.
Splitting data across machines by a key so writes and storage scale horizontally.
A client-supplied ID stored with a request's result so a retried request returns the first result instead of acting twice.
A rate-limiting algorithm: a bucket of capacity C refills at r tokens per second and each request takes one, allowing short bursts.
Fetching relevant documents at query time and putting them in the prompt so the model can answer from them and cite them.
A protocol (Anthropic, 2024) for exposing tools, resources and prompt templates from servers to model applications.
The share of an answer's claims supported by the retrieved sources; measured separately from retrieval recall and answer correctness.
An exact attention algorithm that tiles the computation in on-chip SRAM with an online softmax, avoiding writing the T×T score matrix to GPU memory.
Attention with softmax replaced by a feature map so cost is linear in sequence length and the state is fixed-size, at some cost in recall.
Attainable throughput is the minimum of peak FLOP/s and arithmetic intensity times memory bandwidth; the ridge point separates memory-bound from compute-bound work.
Clustering by alternately assigning points to the nearest centre and moving centres to their points' mean; a hard-assignment limit of a Gaussian mixture.
A density that is a weighted sum of Gaussians, fitted by expectation–maximisation with soft cluster responsibilities.
